title: Rabbi Romanos
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi’s student, as in [Yevamot 60b:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.60b.15): “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: There was a town in the Land of Israel (in the Jerusalem Talmud, Bikkurim 1:5, Yevamot 8:2 and Kiddushin 4:6, the reading is: an incident with a family in Rhodes, or in the South) about which a challenge [to its lineage] was raised, and Rabbi sent Rabbi Romanos, who examined it.”

In [Shabbat 47a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.47a.2), Rabbi Zeira cites Rabbi Assi, who cites Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Chanina. Rabbi Chanina cites Rabbi Romanos: “Rabbi permitted me to move a fire-pan with its ashes.”

In Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:11: Rabbi sent Rabbi Romanos to Antoninus to build him an altar (Hyman regards this as complete proof that the Rabbi who was Antoninus’s friend is our holy Rabbi). Hyman cites Nedarim 31a (compare [Nedarim 38a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.38a.15)): “Rabbi Romanos said: The fare of the ship (of Jonah) was four thousand gold dinars”; Hyman explains that this is not a comment on Rabbi Yochanan’s words, but follows them in the Talmud’s arrangement.[^3]

notes.text: The complete-proof claim about Antoninus is Hyman’s argument about which Rabbi was his friend, not an identification of Antoninus as Rabbi. His statement-sequence explanation distinguishes Romanos’s saying from a comment on Yochanan.

Yevamot 60b directly records Rabbi sending Romanos to examine a town’s lineage. Hyman’s Jerusalem Talmud family, Rhodes/South and Antoninus reports, and the complete-proof argument about which Rabbi was Antoninus’s friend, remain attributed; those exact parallel passages were not independently inspected.

The Yevamot report says that Rabbi sent Romanos to investigate a challenge to a family’s lineage. In the linked Nedarim passage, Rabbi Yochanan says that Jonah paid for the whole ship, and Romanos gives its fare as four thousand gold dinars. Hyman discusses how the two statements are related.
